question: Is everyone on the Titanic okay?
period_answer: Most papers dated April 15 reported that the Titanic had struck an iceberg but that her passengers were safe: they were being transferred to the Carpathia and the Parisian, and the Titanic, badly damaged but afloat, was being towed toward Halifax by the Allan liner Virginian (Barre Daily Times: "All the passengers safe; the Titanic taken in tow"; Lakeland Evening Telegram; Rock Island Argus: "probable all passengers on the Titanic are safe"; Daily Gate City; Seattle Star). White Star officials said the ship was unsinkable and would reach port. A few reports said she was sinking, and one late edition (Washington Evening Star) reported fifteen hundred missing and believed drowned, with about 675, mostly women and children, saved by the Carpathia, and printed a White Star message that the Titanic had foundered.

question: Is HBOS going to be taken over?
period_answer: No takeover had been reported by the end of September 16. HBOS, owner of the Halifax and Britain's biggest mortgage lender, had lost more than a third of its value at one point on September 15 (closing 17.5% down) and its shares fell as much as 40% at one point on September 16, amid worries about its reliance on wholesale funding; HBOS insisted it was a strong bank with significant capital resources. Lloyds TSB shares rose on talk of stakebuilding.
future_facts: Lloyds TSB was reported to be in merger talks with HBOS on the morning of September 17; a £12bn takeover of HBOS by Lloyds TSB was agreed on the evening of September 17; Lloyds TSB confirmed it was paying £12.2bn for HBOS, with thousands of job losses expected (September 18)
